# Module overview {#sec-m5}

::: {.modulo-meta}
**Workload:** 6 hours (3h synchronous + 3h asynchronous)\
**Dates:** 26/10 and 27/10 (synchronous); 23/10 (asynchronous)\
**Packages:** Quarto, `rmarkdown`, `knitr`, `gt`, `r5r`, `gtfstools`, `accessibility`, `aopdata`, `stplanr`, `flownet`, `mapgl`\
**Final project:** an HTML accessibility report for one of five cities (Belo Horizonte, Fortaleza, Porto Alegre, Rio de Janeiro or São Paulo), with interactive maps in `mapgl`
:::

## What you will be able to do by the end of the module

- Write a document that **updates itself** when the data change: text, tables,
  charts and maps produced by the same code.
- Export to HTML, PDF and Word, without redoing the work.
- Compute multimodal travel time matrices and isochrones with `r5r`, and compare
  public transport network scenarios by editing the GTFS.
- Show each step of an accessibility analysis in interactive maps with `mapgl`.
- Deliver an analysis that someone else can run again. That is the goal of the whole
  course.

## Outline

### Synchronous class (3h)

| Block | Content | Chapter |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | Public transport routing with `r5r` and GTFS | @sec-m4-gtfs |
| 2 | Multimodal routing, scenarios and isochrones with `r5r` | @sec-m4-r5r |
| 3 | Flow networks and assignment (`flownet`, `stplanr`) | @sec-m4-r5r |
| 4 | Quarto: structure, figures, tables, cross-references, formats | @sec-m5-quarto |

The maps that go into the reports follow what was seen in @sec-m2-mapas.

### Asynchronous content (3h)

| Block | Content | Chapter |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 5 | Final project: accessibility report for one of five cities | @sec-m5-projeto |
| 6 | Good practice and next steps | @sec-m5-proximos-passos |

## Module packages


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
pacotes <- c("quarto", "rmarkdown", "knitr", "gt", "kableExtra",
             "ggspatial", "patchwork", "scales", "classInt", "mapgl",
             "r5r", "gtfstools", "accessibility", "aopdata", "stplanr")

faltando <- setdiff(pacotes, rownames(installed.packages()))
if (length(faltando) > 0) install.packages(faltando)

# flownet is not yet on CRAN
# remotes::install_github("SebKrantz/flownet")
```
:::


To export to PDF, you need a LaTeX distribution. The simplest is the one R itself
installs:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tinytex::install_tinytex()
```
:::


::: {.callout-important}
## `r5r` needs Java 21

`r5r` is an interface to R5, Conveyal's routing engine, written in Java. Without
**JDK 21** installed, the package loads but fails when building the network. Check before the
session:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# in the system terminal
# java -version    -> should answer "21"

# inside R
rJava::.jinit()
rJava::.jcall("java/lang/System", "S", "getProperty", "java.version")
```
:::


If installation depends on the Ministry's IT team, ask for **JDK 21 (Temurin or Oracle)** in the same
ticket as R and Rtools.

On the first network it builds, `r5r` downloads the R5 engine (a `.jar`) from GitHub, and the Ministry's
network may block that *download*. The step-by-step guide to download it by hand is in
@sec-r5r-jar.
:::

## About the blocks this site does not run

The chapters of this module are run when the site is built, with one declared
exception: the blocks that depend on **`r5r`** require JDK 21 and a folder with the OpenStreetMap `.pbf`
and the city's GTFS: files that do not fit in the repository. These blocks are
marked as not run and give, in the text, the expected result.

To run them on your machine, the `dados/brutos/fortaleza/` folder already comes ready in module 4's data
package, downloaded by the setup script (@sec-m4-osm). To build it by hand, or for
another city:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
dir.create("dados/brutos/fortaleza", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# 1. road network (OSM): there is no Ceará-only extract; the Northeast one comes, about 450 MB.
#    For r5r it is too heavy: the module package has only the Fortaleza region,
#    already cropped (fortaleza.osm.pbf, 54 MB)
osmextract::oe_download(
  file_url = osmextract::oe_match("Ceará")$url,
  download_directory = "dados/brutos/fortaleza"
)

# 2. GTFS: download from https://dados.fortaleza.ce.gov.br (tag "gtfs")
#    and save the .zip in the same folder, without unzipping
```
:::


The `r5r` chapter with Porto Alegre (@sec-m4-gtfs) does not need this folder: it uses the data
that come inside `r5r` itself.
